problem_markdown: Inside square $ABCD$, construct equilateral triangles $ABK,BCL,CDM,DAN$. Prove that the midpoints of $KL,LM,MN,NK,AK,BK,BL,CL,CM,DM,DN,AN$ form a regular dodecagon.
solutions_markdown:
Take $A=(1,1),B=(-1,1),C=(-1,-1),D=(1,-1)$ and set $k=(\sqrt3-1)/2$. Then $K=(0,-2k),L=(2k,0),M=(0,2k),N=(-2k,0)$. The first four midpoints are $(\pm k,\pm k)$, at angles $45^\circ+90^\circ j$ from the origin.

Put $h=1/2$ and $v=(2-\sqrt3)/2$. The other eight midpoints have coordinates $(\pm h,\pm v)$ or $(\pm v,\pm h)$. Since $h^2+v^2=2k^2$, they have the same radius as the first four. Also $v/h=2-\sqrt3=\tan15^\circ$. Altogether the twelve angles are $15^\circ+30^\circ j$ for $0\le j<12$, proving regularity.
